title: Sophistry does not erase clarity — tradition and councils face the same heretical pushback
source_text: XLVII. Respondeo sophisticas & perversitatem hominum qui veritatem negant, atque illi obstrepunt, & mendaciis atque erroribus faciunt aliquem fucum, qui possit homines leves & incautos decipere, non obstare quominus veritas clara & certa sit respectu eorum qui rem debite considerant, & oculo purgato, absque praejudiciis & pravis affectibus. Alioqui nihil prorsus clarum, & certum remanebit. Et dicendum erit non posse ex naturali rectae rationis lumine probari Deum esse, & illum esse unicum, quia Athei & sophistae multi ista negarunt, & ratione abusi sunt ut contrarium astruxerunt: nec ipsis Mathematicis disciplinis constabit sua certitudo atque evidentia, qua Sceptici conati sunt illarum certitudinem evertere: & multis sophismatis & fallacibus argumentis earum principia & axiomata reddere dubia. Et quod magis urgere potest Pontificios, probabo similiter ex traditione & verbo non scripto, non satis clare & certo deduci illa ipsa dogmata, quae in exemplum allata sunt, adeoque praeter verbum ab Apostolis partim scripto partim viva voce traditum, necessarium esse in Ecclesia aliud Dei verbum, unde possint clarius & certius haberi. Nam Ariani & Pelagiani non tantum ex Scripturis disputabant contra Orthodoxos, sed etiam Ecclesiae traditionem sibi vendicabant, & sententiam suam testimoniis priscorum Ecclesiae Doctorum confirmari gloriabantur; ut manifestum est ex veterum contra haereticos illos disputationibus. Imo nequidem res poterit ipsorum Conciliorum authoritate definiri. Nam Orthodoxorum Conciliis sua quoque Concilia Ariani opponebant, ut Ariminense Niceno. Praecipue vero Graeci cum Ecclesia Romana certantes de processione Spiritus sancti a Patre solo, de Monarchia Papae, & aliis articulis, non tantum ex Scripturis pugnant, sed etiam ex antiqua Ecclesiae traditione, ex Patrum testimoniis, & decretis Conciliorum, & Ecclesiae Romanae suam Ecclesiam, traditioni illius suam traditionem, & Concilia sua Conciliis illius opponunt.
pass_a_gloss: I answer that the sophistries and perversity of men who deny the truth, and clamor against it, and with lies and errors make some varnish which can deceive light and unwary men, do not hinder that the truth be clear and certain with respect to those who duly consider the matter, and with a purged eye, without prejudices and wicked affections. Otherwise nothing at all clear and certain will remain. And it will have to be said that it cannot be proved from the natural light of right reason that God is, and that he is one, because many Atheists and sophists have denied these things, and have abused reason to build the contrary: nor will even the Mathematical disciplines keep their certainty and evidence, which the Sceptics have tried to overturn: and by many sophisms and fallacious arguments to render their principles and axioms doubtful. And what can press the Pontificians more, I will prove likewise from tradition and the unwritten word, that those very dogmas which were brought as examples are not deduced clearly and certainly enough, and so that besides the word delivered by the Apostles partly by writing partly by living voice, another word of God is necessary in the Church, whence they can be had more clearly and certainly. For the Arians and Pelagians disputed against the Orthodox not only from the Scriptures, but also claimed the tradition of the Church for themselves, and boasted that their opinion was confirmed by the testimonies of the ancient Doctors of the Church; as is manifest from the disputations of the ancients against those heretics. Nay the matter cannot even be defined by the authority of their Councils. For to the Councils of the Orthodox the Arians also opposed their own Councils, as Rimini to Nicaea. And especially the Greeks contending with the Roman Church about the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father alone, about the Monarchy of the Pope, and other articles, fight not only from the Scriptures, but also from the ancient tradition of the Church, from the testimonies of the Fathers, and the decrees of Councils, and oppose their Church to the Roman Church, their tradition to its tradition, and their Councils to its Councils.
pass_b_english: Sophistry and varnish that snare the unwary do not make truth unclear for a purged, unprejudiced mind.
Otherwise nothing stays certain — not even God's existence by reason, nor mathematics against Sceptics.
Retorsion: the same dogmas are also contested from tradition and the Fathers — Arians and Pelagians claimed tradition too.
Councils do not escape: Arians set Rimini against Nicaea; Greeks oppose Rome with their own tradition, Fathers, and councils.
